articleTitle: Review of Smart Street Lighting Research in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Street lighting is a necessity in open spaces especially roadside. The longer the road in a city, the number of street lighting needed become much more and it makes the government spends much more money to pay the electricity bills. One of the efforts usually used to reduce the electricity cost is by changing the commonly used street lamp to a more energy-efficient lamp such as LED (Light Emitting Diode). In the cities which have moved towards to the smart cities concept such as Jakarta in Indonesia, the technology used for street lighting is smart street lighting (SSL). The street lighting is equipped with a system consisting of sensors, communication devices, and energy management to make the street lighting become automatically adaptable to the environment. It reduces the electricity bill more effective than just only changing the lamp to LED. The use of SSL in Indonesia cannot be separated from the research which had been done and is still being developed about it. The research about smart street lighting in Indonesia had been conducted by some researchers with generally taking the topic about lighting controller and monitor development and the effectiveness comparison between the use of SSL and general street lighting. This paper reviews SSL research which had been carried out by researchers in Indonesia.

articleTitle: LCOE vs PV Penetration in Indonesia De-dieselization Program
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The conversion of fossil fuel power plants to green and renewable power plants has been gaining traction in many countries to ensure access to an affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy source. Recently, the de-dieselization program is one of the programs carried out by the Government of Indonesia through its state-owned electricity company, namely PLN, to convert diesel-powered electricity to green and sustainable hybrid PV-BESS power plants to electrify their remote and off-grid islands. However, this investment in hybrid PV-BESS power plants needs to be analyzed to see its attractiveness compared to the local electricity tariff. One of the methods is by analyzing the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) of the hybrid Diesel-PV-Battery that is proposed in the de-dieselization program. As PV is variable renewable energy, the amount of PV penetration that goes into the system will highly depend on the size of the BESS. The higher PV penetration, the higher the BESS capacity which, therefore, the higher the LCOE. This paper studies the LCOE of the hybrid diesel-PV-BESS power plant with variation of PV penetration that can go into the system. From this study, it can be observed that it is essential to determine the PV-Battery capacity to achieve the lowest LCOE for a specific PV penetration. It also can be noted that when the PV penetration goes beyond 90%, especially if it goes to 100%, there is a substantial increase in LCOE since the PV-Battery required capacities also increase significantly. In this study, the optimum value of LCOE is 33.5 cUSD/kWh. This optimum LCOE can be achieved in 97% PV penetration with PV capacity of 12,118 kWp, PCS capacity of 8,250 kWh, and battery capacity of 24,750 kWh.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Energy Management System For Small-Scale Hybrid Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper explains the energy management system (EMS) to arrange small-scale renewable energy (RE) power plants in one affordable area. RE power plants integrated are sourced from local area such as hydro, biogas, and solar. Hydro power and biogas were built in 2014 with standalone mode, whereas solar power were built in 2015. The main problem is that the energy sources of all existing RE power plants are not continuously available (intermittent). Solar energy is only available during the day. Likewise with water energy sources that was suficient in the rainy season but drastically reduced in the summer. The source of biogas energy is very dependent on the amount of gas content produced from livestock. Therefore an energy system integration arrangement is needed to solve the above problems. The design of integration is done by adjusting the output of each generator source into a DC voltage system to be stored first in the energy storage unit such as batteries. This is due to the simpler and safer arrangement of DC source integration compared to AC source systems. Local grid designed of electrical energy distribution can also be connected with utility grid (on-grid mode) to compensate the intermittent conditions of RE power plants. Finally the design is implemented to maintain energy balance of supply - demand, reduce the grid electricity cost with RE penetration, improve efficiency, security, and reliability of the local grid.

articleTitle: A Review on Asset Health Management and Criticality Parameters in PLN Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: PT PLN (Persero) is naturally exposed to asset risk as an asset-intensive business. To predict the asset risk, PLN needs to understand asset health and criticality. Therefore, PLN needs rigid asset health management (AHM) and criticality parameters aligned with corporate objectives. This paper provides a preliminary review of the current asset health management and criticality parameters in PLN. The methodology to review is through interviews with stakeholders from generation, transmission, distribution, and power systems. The preliminary review found varying approaches across different streams in PLN. One reason for this variation is probably because these initiatives formerly came from the operational rather than from a top-to-bottom direction. Therefore a high-level process for AHM and an initiative to bring together different approaches taken by each stream is suggested. The paper also summarizes development progress on asset risk projects in PLN.

articleTitle: Network Vulnerability Risk of Power Grid Under Intentional Transmission Attacks
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The broad transmission network is vulnerable to physical intention attacks, and its failure would cause load shedding or blackouts for the power grid. Transmission expansion planning currently considers not only N-1 criterion, but also risk. Using game theory model analysis with power flows and probabilistic risk analysis, this study proposes a novel technique for determining a network's susceptibility to intentional transmission attacks, but with a specific focus on the attacker's tactics. This novel approach is a novel formulation of an intelligent attack algorithm for constructing the optimal attacker strategy using DIg SILENT and python. The model is implemented on a modified IEEE 14 and IEEE 39 bus test system with a total peak load of 259 MW and 6,079.1 MW respectively. The network vulnerability risk results in 112.13 MW (37.4% of 14 bus total load) and 298.79 MW (49.15 % of 39 bus total load), indicating that the study network is highly vulnerable to intentional transmission attacks. Future studies will look into the defender's response to complete the game theory of infrastructure security and suggest its application to real-world power system scenarios.

articleTitle: Anti -slip Design for Single Wheel Roller Rig System with Two-Stages Torque Limiter
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper presents a wheel anti-slip control design and experiment for train applications. A wheel slip is a condition where the wheel's linear speed is faster than the train's linear speed, mainly occurring during the acceleration or contaminant on the rail. Some papers explain that torque control in train applications cannot be done with conventional control, but those papers do not explain how to design anti-slip control in detail. A paper also designs the system to work at the maximum adhesion area to maintain the torque limiter. However, it does not explain if wheel slip occurs outside that area. In this paper, we designed an anti-slip control with the torque limiter method, which has two stages so that there is a limiting mechanism if the optimal area of adhesion is missed. The motor is PMSM (permanent magnet synchronous motor), and the controller is coded at MATLAB Simulink environment with Dspace interface. The experimental results show that the two-stage control method runs well and can minimize wheel slip speed.

articleTitle: Loss Analysis of 3-level LLC Converter with Duty Control
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: In this paper, loss models of a Si IGBT system with a switching frequency of 10kHz and a SiC MOSFET system with a switching frequency of 100kHz are derived in a 3-level LLC converter with duty control, and the results are analyzed. Switching and conduction losses of power semiconductor devices are modeled, and losses are analyzed in the proposed circuit system. The loss model mathematically derived through analysis is compared and analyzed with the Psim simulation, and its validity is verified through similarity verification. In addition, it proves the possibility of miniaturization and weight reduction of the auxiliary power supply for railroad vehicles from the derived results.

articleTitle: A Reliable Nested Neutral-Point-Clamped (RNNPC) Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The nested neutral-point-clamped (NNPC) converter suffers from the shoot-through fault similar to other traditional multilevel power converters. To cope with this issue, this paper proposes a novel topology based on the split/coupled inductor concept called a reliable nested neutral-point-clamped (RNNPC) converter. Unlike some previous split/coupled inductor topologies that happening open-circuit fault will cause drastic damage to the converter due to disconnection of inductors' currents, the proposed RNNPC converter can handle this fault resiliently even if all switches are turned OFF simultaneously. Thus, the proposed converter is a highly reliable and robust structure. Higher output voltage/current gain, and lower output voltage/current distortion are other main merits of the RNNPC topology. Detail analysis along with simulation results are provided to verify the feasibility of the new topology.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Partial Discharge Sensor by Combination of Bowtie and Long Bowtie Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Electromagnetic waves is generated when partial discharge (PD) occurs in power apparatus. One of the sensors commonly used in partial discharge detection is the UHF (ultra-high frequency) sensor such as bowtie and long bowtie antenna. In this research, the combination of bowtie and long bowtie antenna is designed and simulated to produce antenna with wider bandwidth. The combination antenna has a bandwidth of 1054.5 MHz which is wider than the bandwidth of individual antenna.

articleTitle: Adaptive Ground Fault Relay Protection for Transformers with Different Neutral Grounding Resistors
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Neutral Grounding Resistor systems can be inserted between the neutral and ground in a power system to provide a ground fault protection through resistance. The fundamental purpose of a Neutral Grounding Resistor (NGR) is to limit the ground fault currents to safe levels so that all the electrical equipment in a power system is protected. Neutral Grounding Resistors are also commonly referred to as Neutral Earthing Resistors and Earth Fault Protection Resistors. This paper will discuss the protection of two parallel HV /MV transformers during normal operating condition and under contigency. Another case discussed is a generator with a different NGR value connected to the MV system. When depicted on a symmetrical components circuit, the short circuit current will vary according to the system operating conditions, either in normal mode or contingency modes. To overcome this, a protection scheme is proposed, which adjusts the settings based on the system's operating conditions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Stability of Large-Scale Photovoltaic Based Generation Integration into Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The recent drought trends and decrease in hydropower generation are alarming to the point where we must plan for an alternate power source to utilize the available transmission line capacity. Interconnection of solar Photo-Voltaic (PV) as a viable electric power supply has been substantially increasing in recent years, making it the most compelling alternate power source to compensate for the loss of hydropower. This paper aims to discuss the dynamic stability of a power system when a large-scale PV -based generation is interconnected to the power system to counteract an increase in load and compensate for drought-impacted hydro generation. For demonstration, a real-world power system is used for this study with permission from Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC). The system is simulated for five scenarios, (I) an existing power system, (II) a system with a 500 MW increase in system load and 500 MW additional PV generation, (III)-(V) a system with 500 MW, 720 MW, and 1440 MW PV generation interconnection to compensate for different levels of decrease in the hydro generation to test different PV penetration levels. The system is simulated with GE PSLF software for various contingencies, and dynamic stability results are reported with fictitious bus names without any Critical Electricity Infrastructure Information (CEIl).

articleTitle: Efficient Smart Grid Data Updating and Diagnostics for Transformer Loading Management
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper develops a business process to maintain a clean Smart Grid data. Such data involves Geographic Infor-mation System (GIS) network data and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) time-series data. For accurate distri-bution transformer optimization, GIS data gap must be managed. Updating and diagnostics of such data must be optimized due to limited metering devices. This paper develop portable tools and design data ecosystem separate from Smart Grid environment for efficient and non-disruptive GIS diagnostics. It takes 33 minutes to build from scratch a fresh network model with customer loads from GIS, Customer and SCADA data. Compared to 42 hours of Smart Grid network model promotion, 98.7% reduction of time in new data build-up for updated diagnostics. Reportorial submission to energy regulatory, efficient system operations, and effective planning relies on GIS accuracy and realtime SCADA availability.

articleTitle: Mathematical Hosting Capacity Calculation due to Arise Voltage using The Equation of Line Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The maximum integration of Photovoltaic Distributed Generation (PDG) into the distribution system without causing a violation is a study related to Distributed Hosting Capacity (DHC). The Hosting Capacity Theorem is used to determine the amount of Photovoltaic Distributed Generation (PDG) capacity for each customer with safe and secure. This Paper can be implemented to fulfill the target of installing clean energy in Indonesia in 2025 in the amount of 23%. This Methodology of Hosting Capacity is installing Photovoltaic in customer-to-customer with the maximum capacity without exceeding the limit system. The contribution of this paper is calculating the voltage increase from the measurement of the load current point at the base (Ip) and the load current point at the end (Iu). This Paper uses the line equation theorem to calculate and obtain the capacity value of the voltage difference in each customer <tex>$(\Delta V)$</tex>. The Different voltages of each customer <tex>$(\Delta V)$</tex> was calculated with accumulation as total values of the rising voltage in the base customer. The results obtained for the load scenario between the same capacity of the customer and the load capacity with different customer capacities. We can the capacity of each customer with the same power factor (PF) values in each customer. This result was validated with the dig silent hosting capacity software results and has a competitive value.

articleTitle: Operational Road Map in North Sulawesi and Gorontalo Power Grid Considering the Intermittent Photovoltaic Penetration
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: In 2019, the North Sulawesi and Gorontalo power system welcomed the gradual entry of photovoltaics into the high voltage grid. The first phase of the solar power plant in North Sulawesi was Likupang PV Plant at 15 MWp and Isimu PV plant at 10 MWp. The North Sulawesi and Gorontalo system is characterized by a daytime peak load of 330 MW. This way, the initial penetration of photovoltaics into the system at this stage is 7.58%. However, the system's nadir stiffness is only within a range of 10–16 MW/Hz. Therefore, the expected frequency fluctuations from intermittent photovoltaics could reach higher than 1 Hz, so it is necessary to re-engineer the operation of the electric power system. This paper presents several stages that PLN as the grid operator needs to develop, starting from the readiness of the SCADA system, adjusting the defense scheme, improving the operation of the system, and PV forecasting. Implementing the photovoltaic curtailment can be an alternative when there is a very high intermittence which causes vulnerability to the system during operation. Developments in the operation scheme and technology for photovoltaics are still carried out in stages, such as using photovoltaics curtails as a reserve margin to energy storage technologies such as the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The aim of the roadmap is to increase system reliability and maximize Photovoltaic utilization

articleTitle: High Efficiency Multiphase Cascaded DC-DC Boost Converters With Inductance Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a multiphase cascaded DC-DC boost converter with high efficiency and optimization of inductance value. The multiphase cascaded DC-DC boost converter is a converter that has a very high gain level and low input current ripple. The study begins with the derivation of the loss equation in the converter, and the results are used for the optimization process. Previous research with the same converter has achieved an efficiency of 85.8%. The selection of inductance value will affect the resistance value of the inductor so that efficiency will increase. However, the winding manufacturing technique and the selection of the inductor core are also determined. By applying the proposed multiphase cascaded DC-DC boost converter with a proper inductor and switching conduction mode, the inverter efficiency can be improved up to 5% which reached 89.19% in laboratory tests. While in critical conduction mode (CRM), at 0.15 mH inductance, efficiency is 86.23%. Experimental work verifies the proposed design and analysis.

articleTitle: Modulated Model Predictive Current Control for Three-Phase NPC Inverter with an LC Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper deals with current control of inverter using modulated model predictive control (MMPC). A traditional model predictive control (MPC) has wide bandwidth and fast dynamic characteristics, but switching state is limited and precise control is difficult. Proposed MMPC eliminates these disadvantages and takes only the advantages of MPC. MMPC shows good performance in applications that require fast dynamic characteristics such as sudden load changes or power failure/recovery. For validation of MMPC, 10kW Three-phase NPC inverter with an LC filter is used. MMPC control for inductor current is performed by simulation and experimental. As a result experiments for MMPC controller, there was almost no steady-state error, and the transient response is fast within 1ms.

articleTitle: PV Intermittent Smoothing with BESS: A Case Study in Selayar Island Electrical Grid
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Solar PV intermittency or variability is one of the major concerns in integrating solar photovoltaic (PV) power plant into an existing electrical grid, particularly a stand-alone grid in remote area that has limited power generation. This paper discusses issues derived from integrating a 1,3 MWp solar PV power plant into Selayar Island electrical grid and simulates grid stability during intermittency while determining the maximum allowable power ramp rate <tex>$(\mathbf{PRR}_{\mathbf{set}})$</tex> for battery energy storage system (BESS) operation. The actual result of smoothing operation in the Selayar electrical grid is then presented to justify the capability of BESS to mitigate the PV solar intermittency.

articleTitle: Hosting Capacity of Solar Power Plant in Java Madura Bali
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Solar power plants are now being developed massively as an alternative energy source. However, integration of high-capacity utility scale solar power plants poses challenges to the existing electricity grid as they generate inconsistent power throughout time, commonly known as intermittency. In this paper, we calculate the potential solar plant capacity that can be injected into the existing grid. The research is conducted by measuring the real sun irradiation in Java, Madura, Bali using 54 measuring devices spread across the islands. The data has been acquired for two months and the intermittency has been observed. The research concludes that if the aggregate irradiation is observed and the Jamali grid stiffness is taken into account, it is possible to interconnect up to 6.67 GW spread across 54 locations.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of The 8/6 SRM Inverters
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper presents detailed analysis, and operation of Asymmetric Half Bridge (AHB) converter topology and shared switch converter topology for 4-phase Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) drives. Compared to an asymmetric half bridge converter, shared switch converter reduces the number of switches and diodes. Simulation results show that both topologies give the same results of phases flux, phases current, torque electric, and speed. However, some switches in shared switch converter controlled more than one phase. So, the number of switching at operation speed condition is twice more than other switches on asymmetric half bridge or shared switch converter. The simulation results are made by MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: The Geographic Smoothing Potential of Solar Irradiation in Java, Madura, and Bali Electric Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Indonesia is making ambitious efforts to increase the usage of renewable energy sources to meet the country's energy needs. However, there were still concerns about how the intermittent nature of solar power output might affect the grid. This study focused on the problem of intermittent solar power and examined the potential role that distributed geographic location could play in lowering the overall intermittency. 18 solar irradiation stations scattered throughout the Java, Madura, and Bali (Jamali) electric power systems were used as the irradiation data source. The total irradiation of all locations was then evaluated for its intermittency using Power Spectral Density (PSD), Welch Method. According to this study, connecting 18 stations reduces intermittency by 70 to 93 percent, depending on the timestep. The study also demonstrates that after 10 locations, the reduction becomes almost insignificant.

articleTitle: Research and Simulation of a new Multi layered material Coupled Inductor
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The paper presents a novel approach to analyzing multi layered material inductors that combine multiple ferrites with different magnetic properties. This work aims to use multi layered material inductors to enable coupled inductors in power converters to flow larger currents without premature saturation of their cores. A research method based on Ansys Maxwell modeling software is validated by comparing the coupled inductance results for a single-material ferrite and a multi layered material ferrite.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Loading on Age Loss and Efficiency on Dry Type Transformer at PT MRT Jakarta
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Transformer is an electric devices and will experience a load which will affect the amount of life shrinkage and also the resulting efficiency. This study aims to analyze the magnitude of life shrinkage, analyze the effect of loading that occurs on dry transformers at the Senayan MRT station and Bundaran HI MRT station. This study has several methods of analysis by calculating the load ratio, temperature hotspot on the transformer, life shrinkage for 24 hours to % relative age loss, and the life of the transformer so that it can find the results of the remaining life of the transformer. Percentage of loading for the Senayan MRT station is between 18.44% and 19.96%, while the percentage of loading for the Bundaran HI MRT station has a higher yield between 32.49% and 34%, respectively. The result of age loss at Senayan MRT station is 0.069% with a remaining life for 15.5465 years. The result of age loss at the Bundaran HI MRT station is 0.15% for 15.5425 years. The efficiency of the result at the Bundaran HI MRT station with an average yield of 99.13%, and at the Senayan MRT station is 98.41%.

articleTitle: Solar Photovoltaic Rooftop Penetration Forecasting Through Bass Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Solar PV Rooftop penetration forecasting into grid is important since the Solar PV is variable renewable energy. The impact analysis of the Solar PV Rooftop penetration both technical and financial will be based on the forecasting results. It can support any decision making on the maximum allowable Solar PV penetration in the grid. Since the installed capacity penetration of Solar PV Rooftop as new advanced technology only supported by limited data history then the Bass Diffusion Model can be proposed to be forecasting method. Combination of Bass Diffusion Model and Monte Carlo Method will give high confidence level of forecasting. It can forecast the total installed capacity in the several scenarios as sensitivity forecasting.

articleTitle: Resistance Analysis of Softwood and Hardwood to the Rotor Speed for Micro-Scale Wind Turbine Blade Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The horizontal axis taper blade with a NACA 4415 airfoil made from Pinus Merkusii as softwood and Swietenia Macrophylla as hardwood has been designed and tested to determine its resistance as a micro-scale wind turbine blade material based on the rotor speed. Softwood and hardwood blades were analyzed by static simulation based on the values of von Mises stress, displacement, and Factor of Safety. The simulation results show that softwood and hardwood blades have good resistance and safety to be used as micro-scale wind turbine blade materials with rotor speeds of 200, 300, and 400 rpm, with Factor of Safety values above 1.0 for both types of wood at all variations of rotor speed. Factor of Safety values for softwood blades are 4.9, 2.3, and 1.3, while hardwood blades are 9.6, 4.5, and 2.5.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Multiphase Modified DC-DC Cuk Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The problem in DC-DC power converters penetrating new and renewable energy is the ripple of high current, non-continuous current, and low efficiency. This paper proposes a multiphase modification DC-DC Cuk converter to obtain a continuous current on the input and output sides with predetermined component values and duty cycles. This power converter proposal aims to get a DC-DC power converter with a continuous input and outputs current, small current ripples, and high efficiency by looking at a fraction of power losses in the converter. The current ripple in this proposed converter is close to zero using a duty cycle value of 0.5, so there is ripple cancellation in the Lm inductor. The largest loss fraction lies in the switch, so efficiency improvements are obtained by replacing the IGBT switch with a MOSFET looking at better specifications. So that an efficiency increase was obtained in the proposed converter by 90.81 % in the B circuit and 90.07% in the C circuit. Verification has been performed from the experiment.

articleTitle: An Interactive Charging Strategy Model between Electric Vehicles and Distribution Electricity Network
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper proposes a charging power load forecasting model for electric vehicle (EV). The factors that affect the charging load are considered. The forecasting curve of electric vehicles charging load distribution is simulated by Monte Carlo method. This model reflects the charging demand of users in different time period. Then, a coordinated interactive charging strategy model based on Genetic Algorithm (GA) is developed. The daily baseload and real-time pricing are introduced. Based on the charging load forecasting curve, considering the grid side and the user side, a variety of optimized charging cases are established. The simulation study results show that this charging strategy not only enables the grid to carry out orderly regulation of charging load, but also guides users to respond to the electricity price and charge in different periods.

articleTitle: Development of Large Scale, End-to-End Online Monitoring Losses (OML)
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The utility companies' main steps in the digital transformation process are asset life cycle management and grid optimization. At these points, efforts to improve the efficiency of the electric power grid are a significant concern. For this reason, utility companies are expected to be able to monitor their operating flow to increase the efficiency of electricity distribution, one of which is by monitoring the losses of the electric power system network. This paper discusses a method for developing an integrated utility end-to-end energy loss monitoring system that monitors the electricity transmission and distribution system online. The method used is to develop an electric power measurement platform according to the local electric power system and consolidate electrical power measurements from measurement points of electric generators, power transmission systems, power transformers, and distribution line feeders. This platform has data communication channels, efficient traffic flow, and high-end database management. The event-driven streaming platform method is a platform that connects all services/ applications in a single data channel (data bus). The advantage of this platform is that it has the capacity for large volumes of data to be communicated in complex systems. On the other hand, it simplifies the communication chain.

articleTitle: The Optimal Electricity Supply Option for Grid Transition of Non-Grid Isolated Island: Case Study Pulau Rengit, Belitung
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The transition of isolated island from non-grid electricity supply to grid connected need the optimal composition of electricity supplies. This research proposes new methodology to answer the needs of grid transition. The methodology contains 2 stages, sequentially. Those are economic analysis and power system analysis. The optimal criterion of economic analysis is minimum LCOE (Levelized Cost of Energy). Whilst the optimal criteria of power system analysis are grid distribution code. The grid distribution code which are implemented will depend on the grid development and its characteristic. However, since the non-grid electricity supply is isolated island, majority, then load flow simulation, short circuit simulation and frequency stability will be mandatory. The iteration is suggesting when the result of the power system analysis don't meet grid distribution code. The power system analysis is mandatory if one of proposed composition is variable renewable energy power plant.

articleTitle: Voltage Responses of Tomia Island Microgrid Under Load Variations
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Constraints on the microgrid, such as demand-supply balance and small inertia on the synchronous machine, require an in-depth study to connect Distributed Energy Resources to the microgrid. Additionally, the power electronic converters that connect the DERs to the microgrid must be regulated and operated differently than the conventional power system. Hence further study has to be made, especially during load variations. Several methods improve a microgrid's stability, such as introducing an energy storage system to the microgrid, a proper control strategy, droop control, load shedding, etc. These methods work best depending on their application and the system scenarios. Tomia Island is one of the islands in Wakatobi Regency, situated in the East of Indonesia. The electricity's high production cost causes the electricity only to be available from 3 pm to 6 am. The limited access of Tomia Island from the nearest power grid caused Tomia Island Microgrid to be isolated from the main grid. The Tomia Island government built four photovoltaic power plants spread across the island to reduce the costs required for Diesel Generators' operation. Thus, this paper analyzes the microgrid behavior, especially the diesel generator's function in maintaining voltage stability during load variations. A 5% Q- V droop control was applied to two out of four PV plants in the Tomia Island microgrid. The result shows that the localized droop control improved the voltage responses on all the PV system points of interconnection due to load loss.

articleTitle: Design of Battery Charger with IoT Capabilities for Electric Bikes
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper describes the design process of a microcontroller-based portable battery charger that has an Internet of Things (IoT) capability to monitor the charging process. A standard DC-DC buck converter is used as power converter to give a DC charging current to a battery, which is controlled by ESP32. At various points of operation, the micro controller can also send various data to a remote server for monitoring purposes via the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) network. It can also send its current location to the server. A rudimentary web dashboard is also made to monitor the charger's state of operation at any given time. The designed system is able to utilize a single microprocessor to simultaneously control the charging process, and also to communicate with the remote server. The charger itself has a maximum output of 650 watts (65.5V, lOA). Experimental works have been done to verify the proposed design

articleTitle: Technical and Economic Viability of PV Power Plants Construction for Rural Area in Nunukan North Kalimantan
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The low reliability of rural power systems is a major problem and continues to pose huge challenges, especially in rural areas. Nunukan is one of the cities in North Kalimantan that directly borders Malaysia. Nunukan is not connected to a high-voltage system, making it have to rely on a conventional power plant. It was found that Nunukan is present in a region with a solar radiation value of 4.329 kWh/m2/day, making it a suitable area for Krayan PV power plant investments. One of the latest renewable energy technologies that can be used is Photovoltaic (PV). In line with the Indonesian government mission since 2020, called GREEN, where in the future, more power plants will be built with renewable energy sources. This study aims to analyze PV power plant construction in Nunukan, North Kalimantan. In addition to electrifying Nunukan, the PV development can also contribute to the ratio of new renewable energy. Assuming the electricity needs around the PV is 540 kWh/day, the planned installation of 396 PV panels with Polycrystalline-type with a capacity of 340-watt peak per panel. The electricity generated will be distributed through an existing network to residents' homes around the plant. When PV power plants are installed on land with high levels of sunlight, longer battery life, and adequate capacity, they make the investment more economically viable. The indicators used as economic valuations are Net Present Value (NPV), Benefit-Cost Ratio (B-CR), and Discounted Payback Period (DPP). The NPV value is positive. Meanwhile, the BCR value is 1.07, and the DPP has a shorter period than the project life. All indicators of economic viability show that the Krayan PV development could be recommended in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Voltage Mode Control for Three-Phase Modified Cuk Inverter
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper analyses a modified Cuk cell for the three-phase inverter. This inverter has advantages such as very low input and output ripple, very low common-mode voltage ripple, does not require a common-mode filter, suitable for microgrid systems, and does not require a filter in the output inverter. The model of the inverter is presented, and then the steady state is derived. Based on the steady-state formula, simple voltage control is proposed. Simulation-based on MATLAB/Simulink is conducted to verify the mathematical analysis and the proposed control.

articleTitle: A Distributed PCS Based DC Microgrid System for Rural Electrification
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Various power plants have been applied to increase electrification in remote areas, one of which is the Centralized Off-Grid PV system with AC micro grid. Although it has been widely used, this system has several drawbacks, including network losses, land, and synchronization with other power plants. A Power Conditioner System (PCS) based distributed generation system with DC micro grid has been proposed to overcome that deficiency. This DC microgrid system consists of multiple Solar DC Towers, each with solar panels, batteries and PCS connected to their respective loads. In the previous papers, an evaluation of the performance of individual PCS has been carried out in several aspects. In contrast, the performance of the entire DC micro grid system when working in multi-point has not been thoroughly tested. In this paper, the performance of a DC microgrid is evaluated in a multi-point system with PV as the primary source. A prototype of a DC microgrid system with two Solar DC Towers has been developed. The system's performance against solar irradiation and its overall efficiency has been tested. The system has also been tested to meet load requirements under various conditions from various sources, including taking and sending power to the DC micro grid with power-sharing mode. The evaluation shows that this DC microgrid system can work appropriately with good system performance, although it can still be improved in the future.

articleTitle: New Single-Phase Voltage Source Inverter Based on Modified Cuk Cell with High Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The application of solar panel in utilizing the generated DC source requires a DC-AC converter (inverter) so that it can be used by the load. In general, conventional inverters have disadvantages, namely square waveforms and high-power losses so that efficiency is small. The general solution that can overcome these shortcomings is to add large filters at the input and output. This paper proposes a voltage source inverter based on modified Cuk cell so that it can produce a sinusoidal output voltage and high efficiency. The proposed topology does not require the additional of input and output filters. Analytical expressions have been derived to confirm the operation of the proposed inverter. Experimental works has been carried out in the laboratory to verify the proposed inverter.

articleTitle: A New Improved Modification of Switched Reluctance Motor 12/8 With Diamagnetic Material
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: In this paper will be reported the modification of the 12/8 conventional switched reluctance motor by inserting pyrolytic graphite to minimize the leakage flux by adding diamagnetic material. The output torque from the proposed modification switched reluctance motor with the addition of pyrolytic graphite produce peak torque at 22.09 Nm increase 10.9% compared to a conventional motor peak torque, while the average torque is 12.67 Nm rise 13.7 %. The new model of rotor geometry is found that adding the pyrolytic graphite have effect on increase the output torque. The future study about shape and position of the pyrolytic graphite should be taken.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Power Factor Characteristic in ILST Fan Drive Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Laboratory for Aerodynamic, Aeroelastic, and Aeroacoustic (LA3) - BRIN is The Government Agency responsible for conducting aerodynamics, aeroelastic and aeroacoustic technology activities in Indonesia. One of the facilities operated by LA3 is Indonesian Low Speed Tunnel (ILST), where the equipment used in ILST consists of a closed wind tunnel, DC electric motor, and DC drive system. The fan drive system uses a parallel DC Drive System, where Master Motor and Slave Motor are connected to the Master Drive System and Slave Drive System, which means each anchor terminal of the two motors is connected in parallel with the driving terminal. This paper presents the evaluation of ILST fan drive power system, especially in term of power factor. To improve the quality of electric power according to related standard, authors evaluate in field and literature study, and also analyze for power factor correction recommendations. It is hoped that this evaluation can improve the quality of the electrical power of the ILST fan drive system, especially in term of power factor (PF) value.

articleTitle: Experiment Results on AC Tracking Resistance of ZnO/Epoxy Microcomposites
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: In order to meet the increased demand for electrical energy, the application of advanced technologies to the power transmission network has increased. Representative examples include HVDC, UHVAC and FACTS. In order to apply such technologies, development and operation of novel power equipment that support fully functionality of such technologies are required. In addition, research on electrical insulation performance is also required to realize safe and stable operation of power equipment. With such background, this paper reports test results of the tracking resistance of epoxy composites filled with micro sized ATH and ZnO particles. Results of the inclined plane test (IPT) showed that micro-composites could show improved tracking resistance performance compared to pure epoxy specimen.

articleTitle: Solar Smart Dome Modelling With Helioscope
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: One of the biggest problems in the food cycle is the food waste. Most of developing country has more share of losses that normally occurs started from the farm to the customer. Furthermore, solar energy become known widely for food preservation. It is one of the first application since the beginning of the manhood beside for the construction and cloths. Although microorganism problems normally occur because of the lack of storage system management, sun drying method is still universally used [1]–[3].

articleTitle: Design and Validation Non-Isolated Boost Converter for Cascaded Photovoltaic Application
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) has been widely used for converting solar energy into electricity. Since the output voltages from the PV module are low (12, 24V), PV panels must be combined into series or parallel configurations to get the desired voltage. However, in such a configuration, a PV module that is not identical to other panels may cause a short circuit or decrease PV power. A cascaded DC-DC converter system can solve this problem. Each output voltage of the panel or sub-string can be controlled separately. A conventional boost converter topology in a cascaded system requires a high duty cycle value. This causes the switching components to heat up quickly, resulting in power losses. Therefore, a proposed DC-DC converter topology with a low-value duty cycle and low component ratings is designed for a cascaded system. One main advantage of the proposed topology is its ability to produce a voltage gain of 3 times the input voltage with a duty cycle of 37%. Theoretical analysis, simulations, and comparison with other conventional converter topologies were carried out to validate the converter's performance.

articleTitle: Calibration of Partial Discharge Sensors in Air and SF 6 Insulation
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: One of important step in the development of partial discharge (PD) sensor and PD measurement is the sensor calibration. The standard used in PD sensor calibration is IEC 60270. PD sensor calibration will produce scale factor k used for converting a value from voltage to charge. This paper deals with the comparison of calibration of four sensors used in PD measurement. Those sensors are RC detector, high frequency current transformer (HFCT), antenna, and transient earth voltage (TEV) sensor. The experiment is carried out using a needle-plate electrode placed in the air medium and in the SF 6 medium, respectively. This experiment produces a conversion factor from the voltage to the charge for each sensor.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Battery Energy Storage Systems in Isolated Grids: Novel Approach to Shave Peaks & Optimize Energy Costs
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Isolated power systems are typically found in rural areas that are far separated from the power grid. Rapid decrease in BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems) cost provides new opportunities and preferences for utilities to store cheap energy at low loads and power out that energy at peak loads. BESS is installed to shave or level demand during peak hours in an isolated system can avoid the use of peaking generations mostly coming from oil fuels. Considering the BESS function for peak shaving, the approach is to simulate the unit commitment of different battery sizes at 10 MW, because the use of oil fuels about 10 MW at peak load, so the simulation will be representing the total energy of the battery needed by the system. Based on the simulation, the life cycle cost is significantly greater than the benefit at all power and energy ratings. The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate the comprehensive technical and financial analysis needs to find the optimum battery type and capacity to provide optimum impact and financially benefit the system with an approach to shaving peaks and energy costs. A study-case method is demonstrated by taking an isolated system as the base and BESS performance can accelerate voltage in the subsystem for every substation when discharging at peak load. The simulation results that 10 MW/10 MWh lithium-ion batteries provide the highest benefit compared to the life cycle cost.

articleTitle: Optimum Microgrid Sizing for Rural Application in Bangko Island, Southeast Sulawesi
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Due to the difficulty of access and the small number of potential users, there are still many rural areas in Indonesia that do not have access to electricity. Microgrid is one solution to this problem. Using their available energy sources directly without connect it to the grid is cheaper. This paper describes the design and optimum sizing of microgrid for the case of Bangko Island from technical and economic point of view. From the simulations carried out using HOMER Pro, a system with PV capacity of 48 kWp, 287 kWh of battery bank, and 22,4 kW converters is the best system to be implemented in Bangko Island with NPC is Rp. 3,385,657,076.

articleTitle: Wind farm layout optimization based on the wind resource grid
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Micro-Siting wind turbines are always prudent considered during project development, detailed design, and construction of wind farms. The turbine's location in projects significantly affects the project finance, land occupied, and environmental impacts. This paper proposes applying wind farm layout optimization based on a wind resource grid, which includes wind characteristics, topographic data, and roughness, using some powerful optimization algorithms published recently. The main objective of this paper is to maximize the annual energy production of the wind farm with a carefully calculated wake-effect. The best optimal layouts, uniformly calculated by WAsP software, show that the method proposed in this paper gives the optimal results competitive with windPRO software. The feasibility of applying the research results to the optimal design of the wind farm is practical.

articleTitle: Interactive Web Application Design of Online Partial Discharge Monitoring Prototype
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper deals with design of prototype of the online partial discharge monitoring system and the comparison of developed system with conventional system. In the conventional method, the partial discharge experiment requires user to understand several steps to extract bulk received data from oscilloscope into easy reading data. In addition, the bulk data from oscilloscope need to be processed in excellent computer because it faces millions point of data and create a nice graph to make a data interpretation. The proposed method aims to substitute all data processing by human into machine algorithm. The prototype of online monitoring partial discharge is the first step for deep analyzing partial discharge phenomena both in artificial and real condition. The bulk data stored in database may be used for diagnosis of insulation condition, remaining life of HV apparatus, etc.

articleTitle: Effects of Amorphous Iron and Supercore as Core Material on Electric Field and Torque Characteristics for 450W 8/6 Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: To prevent dependency to permanent magnet material for electric machinery construction, there has been an increase on SRM research to enhance its characteristic to be able to compete against permanent magnet motor. In this paper, different core material is tested to see how it will improve SRM characteristics. High silicone steel, also known as super core and new material, Amorphous iron is compared to conventional laminated steel on 450W SRM usually used for household appliance. Finite element method is used to analyze torque and magnetic field characteristics. From simulation, it is concluded that amorphous iron and super core is proven to be able to increase maximum torque and average torque by increasing magnetic field. However, this new material is also shown to increase torque ripple and potentially increase noise.

articleTitle: The Experience of Heavy Water Contaminated Power Transformer Field Repairing Using Combination Method of Hot Oil Circulating and Hot Oil Spraying
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Water contamination can cause accelerated aging of cellulose material, decreased dielectric strength of insulation, and a risk of bubble evolution at high temperatures, which can cause dielectric breakdown. In the heavy water contamination condition, the water content may exceed the saturation level and water will appear in the form of droplets, commonly known as free water. This free water then evolves into sediment that can be found and dispersed on the core surface, the bottom of the tank, radiators, wooden construction elements, etc. Several methods to deal with water contamination in transformers include hot oil spray and hot oil circulation. This paper will elaborate on the experience of a power transformer field repair process that experienced heavy water contamination. The discussion includes the background of contamination occurrence, measurement testing to detect contamination, and the repair process using a combination method of Hot-Oil Spray and Circulating Hot-Oil. The methods in this research were used to prove that this mechanism can preferably be recommended to overcome such heavy water contamination problems.

articleTitle: Power Flow Analysis of DC Train Substation System
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The increased number of electric train passengers causes the increased number of DC electric train trips. The increased number of DC electric train trips must be supported by the capability of DC train substations. So, the DC train substation system needs to be analyzed for its power flow. The power flow analysis of the DC train substation system is more complex than the conventional network because electric trains have dynamic load characteristics. This paper presents the power flow analysis for a DC train substation system with the characteristics of the mechanical and physics sides of train motion. Calculation of power flow using the Current- Inj ection method, and with headway variations in the morning and afternoon peak loads. The DC train substation analyzed in this paper is Pasar Minggu, modeled with the two closest DC train substations. The calculation results show that with headway variations, the highest power of traction transformer and silicon rectifier occurring during the morning peak load, the highest catenary drop voltage is still within tolerance limits, and the electric train operates normally.

articleTitle: Simulation of Simple Grid-connected System Based on PV Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: This paper describes the research found and design processes that implemented while developing Three-Phase Inverter System. The report will begin with research on inverters, inverter control, and components used in this design. This article explores methods and possibilities for implementing low-cost photovoltaic grid-connected power generation systems. This system can meet the needs of on-campus teaching and small-scale distributed power generation.

articleTitle: The Optimal Integration of Small Scale Wind Turbine to The Low-Inertia Grid: Case Study 3 Nusa Grid, Nusa Penida
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The isolated island grid is part of low inertia grid. Penetration of renewable energy, especially variable renewable energy, like solar energy and wind energy will increase the contribution of renewable energy to energy mixed and so do reduce the carbon emission. However, the integration of wind power plant should meet 2 criteria following (1). Decreasing electricity production cost and (2) Keep grid performance in allowable parameter during any disturbances. In this research, the 2 steps method propose to overcome the constraint in renewable energy development. The 1<sup>st</sup> method is LCOE, and 2<sup>nd</sup> method is frequency stability, sequentially. On the case study in grid 3 Nusa, Nusa Penida, the electricity production cost will decrease following decreasing of LCOE. Whilst the grid frequency can keep in the allowable frequency during selected disturbance when 4 MW small scale wind turbine integrate to the grid. Therefore, the combination of the 2 methods, sequentially will produce the optimal sizing for penetration of wind turbine power plant into low inertia grid, like isolated island.

articleTitle: Contingency Analysis of Electric Power Flow as a Power System Operation Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The electric power distribution system from power plants to electric power loads is designed in such a way that it is an efficient grid system. Changes in load at any time result in changes in the amount of power generated. Likewise, on the other hand, changes in generating power will also change the flow of power from the generator to the load. Contingency analysis is intended to determine the condition of the power flow as a result of the discharge of a line to the network or other lines. Contingency selection is carried out to determine the severity of a network by calculating the line performance index (IP) value. The power flow calculation is carried out using the Newton-Raphson method. The results obtained obtained 5 lines that have a higher IP than the slack bus, so the 5 lines are simulated by removing the line from the power flow model. It is also obtained that these 5 lines affect the power flow of other lines, also increasing the generation of reactive power and power losses in the lines.

articleTitle: Integration of Battery Energy Storage System to Increase Flexibility and Penetration Renewable Energy in Indonesia: A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: In recent years, emissions reduction to mitigate the worst effects of climate change has emerged as a primary objective shared by world organizations. Along with the high demand for electrical energy in Indonesia and the policy of raising the electrification ratio to 100 percent by the year 2025, it is anticipated that the electricity demand will expand more than seven times to a total of 1,611 TWh in the year 2050. Boosting the integration renewable energy sources (RES) is a step toward net-zero emissions and contributes as a source of energy supply in the electricity generation process. However, the problem arises because RES especially solar and wind energy are intermittency, highly dependent on nature, and leading to unstable load power supply risk. Using a battery energy storage system (BESS) is one way to overcome instability in the power supply and increase flexibility and RES penetration in Indonesia. This study will briefly discuss how implementing BESS can increase the flexibility and concentration of RES in Indonesia. Examining the trend and challenges in developing the BESS of the scope views the proposed future direction to implement BESS in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Characterization of Energy Saving Lamps in Indonesia Based on Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: The use of energy-saving lamps in Indonesia is increasing continuously. Currently, the use of LED lamps in residential is only 52 %. While the use of CFL lamps is 41 % and the incandescent lamp is 7%. Research on energy-saving lamps has resulted in several driver topologies for LED and CFL lamps. With the application of these topologies, energy-saving lamps can be categorized as non-linear loads that produce harmonic components. This paper will describe the characterization of several types of energy-saving lamps, such as LED and CFL which are still widely used in Indonesia. Measurements in this study use a Power Analyzer to determine the impact of using energy-saving lamps on Power Quality. In addition, another test is conducted to investigate lamp efficiency on luminance and active power to investigate lamp performance. The measurement results on several brands of lamps show that there are four different types of waveforms in LED lamps and one waveform in CFL lamps. Some types of LED have the same waveform as CFLs but have different power capacities with the same lumen range. At the same time, the four types of LED have different power factors and current levels. Then, the result of lamp efficacy shows that LED has a higher value than an incandescent lamp and CFL, so the characterizations of energy-saving lamps can be seen based on their efficiency and power quality.

articleTitle: Multi-aspect Assessment of Municipal Solid Waste Co-Firing Compared to Waste to Energy Plant Projects in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)

authors.preferredName: I Gde Agung Chandra Satriya Wibawa

abstract: Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) management still exists as a major problem in several cities in Indonesia. In 2018, the Indonesian government accelerated the WTE program by releasing specific regulations about the construction of a WTE plant in 12 cities. In 2019, almost all WTE plant projects were delayed because of several problems such as investment funds, high processing technology and lack of competency. Another big problem is about the electricity generated from WTE plants charged at a premium price. Co-firing program which processes raw MSW into pellets and burns it together with coal in a Coal Fired Power Plant (CFPP) can be an alternative solution to solve MSW management problems and help the government catch up to their national energy mix target. This paper will be focused on assessing some aspects which can be used to compare between co-firing MSW and building a WTE plant, including technical, environmental and economic aspects. Technical aspects assess the effect on boiler parameters when MSW was added to be mixed with coal in several proportions. Environmental aspects examining whether essential pollutant parameters comply with government regulation while economic aspects evaluate cost of capital and operational expenditure. After doing a multi-aspect assessment, the result shows that co-firing MSW pellets with coal is a better alternative option compared with building a WTE plant to solve the MSW management problem.

articleTitle: Demand-Side Management in Microgrids: Between Theories and Practical Approaches
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Currently, demand variation problems in power systems are mostly solved from the generation perspective. Fluctuating load demand is a challenge for operators to manage generator dispatch in order to achieve a balance of supply and load. On the other hand, the potential of demand-side management (DSM) has not been explored much as an alternative paradigm in power system control and operation. In fact, the demand management approach is promising because it offers a much cheaper solution than the investment and operation of additional power plants. Load growth which is much faster than the growth of power plants, is a rational reason to start thinking about how to manage the load effectively so that the system operates efficiently. This paper reviews the development of demand-side management (DSM), which has actually been around for a long time, and the extent to which the techniques and solutions have been put into practice. Furthermore, various DSM techniques in renewable energy-based microgrids currently developing rapidly are also discussed.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of Nuclear-Biogas-Solar Hybrid Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Power Engineering and Renewable Energy (ICPERE)
abstract: Utilization of new and renewable energy sources is currently one of Indonesia government's intensified agendas, especially for increasing the electrification ratio and providing green power generations in Indonesia. Indonesia has many potentials of gifted natural resources which can be used to expand national electricity supply. This paper proposes a hybrid electric power plant that adopts three energy sources (nuclear, biogas, and solar thermal) as the primary energy source. A sodium cooled nuclear reactor, typical biogas and solar thermal plant are selected for verifying the concept by using Ebsilon Pro commercial software. The result shows that efficiency of the nuclear alone power plant, biogas alone power plant and solar thermal alone power plant are 35.40%, 32.66%, and 38.97%, respectively. These efficiencies can be significantly improved by adopting the proposed nuclear, biogas, and solar thermal hybrid power plant. The thermal efficiency of the power plant can be enhanced to 40.42 % in term of first law efficiency.
